newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Abacha aide escapes bomb attack in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Abacha aide escapes bomb attack in Nigeria.

text.p: An army colonel who is one of the closest aides of Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha narrowly escaped a bomb blast on Monday and police said they did not rule out political motives for the attack.

Colonel Muhammed Marwa, the military administrator of Lagos state, was not hurt but the explosion seriously injured two security men sitting in the last car of the convoy in which he was travelling as well as a civilian bystander.

"We have left all doors wide open in our investigation, I am not saying it is NADECO and we are investigating all possible motives," Police Commissioner Abubakar Tsav told Reuters. NADECO (National Democratic Coalition) groups human rights and pro-democracy activists opposed to the military government.
Tsav said six suspects had been arrested including one man who was found lying in the gutter near the site of the blast on the Opebi link road.
People at the scene said those arrested included flower sellers who had a stall nearby.
The bomb, which Tsav said had the explosive power of five kg (11 lb) of TNT, blew a small crater in the road and scattered concrete fragments which hit a hotel 100 metres (yards) away.
"The bomb disposal expert says it was propbably triggered by remote control," Tsav said.
"The administrator was not injured, we thank God," he said.
Witnesses said the colonel, who served as Nigeria's defence attache in Washington until August, was clearly the target of the attack but escaped by a whisker.
"The car in which Colonel Marwa was riding had just passed and the vehicle hit was the last in his entourage," said Ibrahim Bello, a communications engineer at the scene.
"The windows of the vehicle were shattered in the back and front," he added.

The News Agency of Nigeria quoted police deputy superintendent Goni Gogo as saying there was a striking similarity between the device that exploded on Monday and a bomb that killed three people last month.

The three, including the head of airport security, were killed in a bungled car bomb explosion in Lagos in November. Police said the victims were agents of the exiled opposition leader and Nobel Prize winner for literature, Wole Soyinka.
Marwa is one of the officers closest to Abacha, who took power in 1993 in the crisis unleashed when a previous military leader annulled a presidential poll that would have restored democracy.

After his assignment in Washington, Marwa was in August appointed administrator of Lagos, the bastion of the opposition symbolised by Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of the annulled poll who has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president.
